newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher but below intraday highs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher but below intraday highs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher, but traders said wheat eased off its intraday highs during the session's second half as fund buying faded, traders said.
Commercials bought wheat early, and traders said that promped active fund buying that took the market to its intraday highs.

But the market's sharply higher tone was short-lived by commercial selling tied to an increase in farmer selling. Traders said farmer sales had picked up in recent days as producers tried to cash in on the rally in wheat prices.
Traders said they had seen some short-covering by locals during the session's second half, but it disappeared toward the close.
"We had lighter volume in the session's last hour and the market just felt tired," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled five to eight cents per bushel higher. September ended up five cents at $3.67-3/4, below its intraday high of $3.72-1/2.

Traders said Rosenthal Collins was among the largest fund-related players, buying 2.5 million Sept bushels. Shay Grain bought 2.2 million Sept, and E. D. & F. Man International bought 1.5 million Sept and 1.1 million Dec. Man also bear-spread one million March/Sept at 21-1/2 to 22-1/2 cents.
Wolcott Lincoln sold at least one million Sept and two million Dec. Farmers Commodities sold two million Sept, and Benson-Quinn sold 1.5 million bushels each of Sept and Dec.
Volume was estimated at 59.940 million bushels, up from 53.265 million bushels Tuesday.
